relations.subject: n1ql:question-mark-positional-placeholder
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - isSynonymOf is a promoted predicate and the page states equivalence in as many words ("an alternative way to specify the same query"). Note both examples return byte-identical results, which corroborates the claim
relations.evidence: Positional parameters can also be specified in a statement using the question mark (?), so the following statement is an alternative way to specify the same query.

relations.subject: n1ql:numbered-positional-placeholder
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted - the registry has requiresSetting (for cluster/node settings) and requiresFlagToEnable (for feature flags) but nothing for "this feature requires that request parameter to be supplied". REST request parameters are a distinct tier from settings - the intro page's own three-tier hierarchy (cluster / node / request) makes that explicit - so requiresSetting would conflate two tiers

relations.subject: n1ql:question-mark-positional-placeholder
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted - see above; both placeholder forms draw their values from the same args array, which is the mechanical basis of their equivalence
relations.evidence:
-d 'statement=SELECT airline FROM `travel-sample`.inventory.route
                   WHERE sourceairport = ? AND distance > ?

notable_absence.finding: No cross-references of any kind - no See Also, no inline links, in particular none to server/current/n1ql/n1ql-manage/query-settings.md where positional parameters are actually specified. Identical absence to exnamed.md; the whole example directory is a cross-reference dead end, linked into only from examplesrest.md.

version_finding: As with exnamed.md, the page's syntax coverage lags the same product version's own reference page. server/current/n1ql/n1ql-manage/query-settings.md documents a mixed numbered form using both prefixes - "WHERE country = $1 AND geo.alt > @2;" with the explanation "the first positional parameter value is used for the placeholder numbered `$1`, the second positional parameter value is used for the placeholder numbered `@2`, and so on" - while this page shows only $1/$2 and ?. So Server 8.0 supports three positional placeholder spellings ($n, @n, ?) and this page exhibits two. No version is attached to the @n form anywhere, so no availableSince relation can be sourced; recording it as the gap. Nothing on this page carries any version or edition marker.
